briefing.opening: Good morning. Welcome to the climate briefing for October 5, 2026. Today's main news covers the severe impacts of climate change reported across the globe, along with various efforts and challenges to overcome them.

sections.title: 🔴 Global Climate Crisis: The Deepening Cry of Nature and Ecosystems
sections.content: The direct impacts of climate change are becoming increasingly visible worldwide. Glaciers in Switzerland have shrunk by approximately 20% in the last five years, signaling a severe warning [2], and over 80% of trees in Luxembourg's forests are facing an unprecedented decline, escalating the ecosystem crisis [38]. Furthermore, marine mammal centers are preparing for prolonged sea lion rescue operations due to deadly toxins caused by climate change [23], and research in Brazil suggests that climate change could silently corrode concrete buildings, threatening even infrastructure safety [29]. Amidst these circumstances, urgent pleas for help are emerging [40], and actor Paul Rudd has also called climate change 'the issue of our time,' urging public awareness [22].

sections.title: ⚠️ International Community Ahead of COP31: A Dilemma of Responsibility and Policy
sections.content: With COP31 just one month away, the international community is facing a deep dilemma regarding its responsibility and policy direction in responding to climate change. Australia and Türkiye, the host nations for COP31, have been criticized for expanding fossil fuels, confronting a 'coal dilemma' [4, 41]. Amnesty International urged world leaders at Pre-COP31 to take action, not just make speeches, for the Pacific region [24]. Meanwhile, major climate change-related lawsuits are set to begin or be heard in the U.S. Supreme Court starting from the new session [14, 16, 25, 28], and Middlesex County has filed a lawsuit against major oil companies to recover climate change damages [31], highlighting corporate accountability. Domestically, concerns have been raised about the 'Carbon Neutrality Act,' with criticisms that the committee's role is negligible, leading to worries about effective policy implementation [6].

sections.title: 🌍 The Shadow of Climate Change Over Human Health and Food Security
sections.content: Climate change poses a severe threat to human health and global food security. Reports continue to emerge that long-term climate change harms human health, to the extent that New Jersey's health crisis has been labeled 'climate change' [20, 21]. It particularly casts a crisis over the education and future of children in coastal areas [26] and directly impacts livelihoods and food security in these regions [37]. In agriculture, France is struggling to finance climate adaptation due to increasing losses [34], and Hungarian paprika farmers face a hotter, drier future, threatening even their culinary traditions [35]. In response to this severity, the World Health Organization (WHO) is participating in Pre-COP31 to promote climate actions that contribute to people's health [27], and a parliamentary group on climate change and migration issues held its first meeting, initiating multi-faceted discussions on the complex crisis [39].

sections.title: 🌱 Domestic and International Efforts Towards Carbon Neutrality and the Hope of Renewable Energy Transition
sections.content: Amidst these crises, diverse domestic and international efforts towards carbon neutrality and the transition to renewable energy offer hope in combating climate change. Domestically, Seoul's Nowon-gu participated in the EU Green Day Festival to showcase its carbon neutrality achievements [3], while Gwacheon City and Naju City are leading carbon neutrality practices by holding local energy plan briefing sessions and being selected as excellent cities/counties for two consecutive years, respectively [7, 8]. Goheung County is ushering in a 10GW renewable energy era and promoting energy transition through a 'citizen grand compromise' [10], and Korea Western Power and Jeonnam Development Corporation are accelerating the development of onshore and offshore wind power in the Gwangju-Jeonnam region [13]. Furthermore, Japan demonstrated technological progress by successfully achieving 'carbon-neutral navigation' using a hydrogen-engine tanker, reducing 1.2 tons of CO₂ in two hours [5]. The market for dry-type transformers and high-speed rotating kinetic energy flywheel systems is projected to accelerate growth until 2035, driven by demand for renewable energy integration [11, 12]. In Colorado, over 1,200 students have earned climate 'certifications,' strengthening the climate action capabilities of future generations [42].

briefing.closing: As we have seen in today's briefing, climate change is having widespread and severe impacts on nature, ecosystems, human health, and society as a whole. At the same time, we have confirmed that the international community's responsible actions and proactive domestic and international efforts towards carbon neutrality and renewable energy transition are continuing in response to this crisis. We urge you to closely monitor international solidarity and domestic implementation for climate change response, and to continue efforts for a better future. This concludes today's climate briefing.
